rationale:
bugs_open/024. No tool-improver fix has EVER reached a live tool page. The loot-table benchmark has failed the same mobile-fit check across three repair cycles since 2026-07-17; each cycle wrote a good fix and reported success. The fixes are all present in content_components.html_template; page_components.rendered_html is still 9,901 chars — the v1 born length — and the live page is byte-identical to birth. So the re-verification could only ever come back RED: the page under test never changed. This was previously diagnosed as fix-loop non-convergence (bugs_open/010, 'the fixer keeps aiming at the wrong element'). That produced a genuine improvement (drill-down attribution) but was not the reason re-verification stayed red.

Three defects in series, each hiding the next, all verified against production:
(1) update_component_html writes the template then only sets page_components.build_status='pending' and relies on 'the rerender pipeline' to regenerate. Nothing in the repo scans pending rows — the codebase says so itself at store_generated_component_action.go:455. The flag is dead state.
(2) tool-improver's own create_rerender_item sets no spec_data, so the item carries no spec.reason. page-rerender's check_rerender_mode gates on exactly that field, so the request always takes else_step -> rerender_single_page, whose own header reads 'Simple concatenation - no template re-rendering'. It assembles the stale stored rendered_html, deploys it, and marks the page 'deployed'. The work item, the orchestration and the page status are all legitimately green over an unchanged page.
(3) Forcing the correct branch by hand (reason=section_data_resolved, item 478c44c9) proved (2) and exposed the last defect: rerender_sections RAN and then ESCALATED instead of rendering, because the content pre-check refuses any section with empty content_data. That guard is the fix for the blanked article bodies (bugs_closed/004, 005) and is correct for its purpose, but a self-contained tool has content_data={} and no input_schema BY DESIGN. check_escalated then routes escalated==true -> complete, bypassing save_sections — the only writer of rendered_html. The render is computed and thrown away, and the page is escalated to a full rebuild, which for a tool page would regenerate and destroy the tool (the known re-plan-clobbers-built-pages landmine; I cancelled that ticket).

Intent: make a durable template fix actually reach the page, by REUSING the pair that store_generated_component already uses correctly for the identical situation, and by teaching the blanking guard the difference between 'has no content' and 'needs no content'. I am deliberately NOT fixing insertWorkItem's two-strike rule here (it counts a COMPLETED rerender as a failed attempt, so two successes poison a site-wide key and later items are born 'unresolved'). It is real and filed, but createRerenderWorkItem inserts via raw SQL and bypasses insertWorkItem, so this change does not depend on it, and mixing them would widen the blast radius of a change I want narrow.

plan.summary: A fix written to content_components.html_template never reaches the rendered page. Make update_component_html REQUEST the re-render (reason=section_data_resolved + component_id) using the existing markPagesPendingRebuild/createRerenderWorkItem pair instead of relying on a build_status='pending' flag nothing reads; stop rerender_page_sections escalating sections whose component declares no required LLM-authored fields (every self-contained tool), which currently discards a good render and asks for a destructive full rebuild; and drop tool-improver's now-redundant, mis-keyed, reason-less create_rerender_item step.

edits.rationale: The action changes the durable template, so it is the correct place to request the re-render — exactly as store_generated_component does. Reuses that file's existing helpers rather than adding machinery: markPagesPendingRebuild performs the same UPDATE and additionally returns the affected site_ids, and createRerenderWorkItem raises a component-scoped item already stamped with the reason and component_id that check_rerender_mode and create_rerender_items both require. Blast radius is one step in the whole fleet: update_component_html is used only by tool-improver.update_component (verified against the live agent_definitions).
edits.sketch:
--- a/platform/orchestration/actions/update_component_html_action.go
+++ b/platform/orchestration/actions/update_component_html_action.go
@@ -248,15 +248,25 @@
-	// --- 4. Mark associated page_components as pending rebuild ---
-	// Do NOT set rendered_html here. ... The rerender pipeline regenerates
-	// rendered_html correctly; we just flag that it needs to run.
-	rebuildResult, err := params.DB.ExecContext(ctx, `
-		UPDATE page_components
-		SET build_status = 'pending', updated_at = NOW()
-		WHERE component_id = $1
-	`, componentID)
-	if err != nil {
-		logger.Warn("UpdateComponentHTMLAction: Failed to update page_components", zap.Error(err))
-	}
-	var pagesMarked int64
-	if rebuildResult != nil {
-		pagesMarked, _ = rebuildResult.RowsAffected()
-	}
+	// --- 4. Mark pending AND REQUEST the re-render ---
+	// build_status='pending' is INFORMATIONAL ONLY: nothing in the repo scans
+	// page_components for pending rows (store_generated_component_action.go:455
+	// says so in its own comment). Flagging alone is why every tool fix since
+	// 2026-07-17 stayed invisible on the live page. Reuse the exact pair
+	// store_generated_component already uses for the same situation.

+	// on. Without them it takes else_step -> rerender_single_page, which is

+	// It also keys per-component (component_regen_rerender:<id>) and inserts
+	// at 'triaged' via raw SQL, so it is unaffected by insertWorkItem's

+	}

edits.rationale: The guard conflates 'this section has no stored content' with 'this section needs stored content'. A component with no required source:'llm' fields renders wholly from its own template, so empty content_data is normal, not dangerous — there is no blanking risk to protect against because there is no LLM content to lose. Probing the contract with missingRequiredLLMFields(schema, nil) reuses the existing predicate as the does-this-need-content test, so the article-body protection is preserved bit-for-bit (article-body declares a required llm field, so it still escalates on both original branches). Without this, a tool page can never be re-rendered at all, whatever the caller asks for.

Once edit 1 lands, this step is not merely redundant but harmful: it raises a SECOND item keyed site-wide (rerender_tool_fix_<domain>, from create_work_item_action.go:128) with no spec.reason, which re-ships stale HTML, and which insertWorkItem's two-strike rule marks 'unresolved' at birth once two prior rerenders have completed. Every such item since 2026-07-18 is unresolved in production. Snapshot first, per the standing rule.

plan.risks:
1) Edit 2 widens what gets re-rendered: sections previously escalated purely for empty content_data will now actually re-render. Check the predicate is right — a component with an input_schema that declares fields but none of them required+source:'llm' will now render rather than escalate. I believe that is correct (nothing required is at risk of being lost) but it is the judgement call in this change and deserves the closest look.
2) Edit 1 makes every update_component_html call raise a rerender work item. Today that is one caller (tool-improver), but a future caller inherits the behaviour — intended, though it should be a conscious inheritance.
3) createRerenderWorkItem defaults workItemSource to 'component-creator'; I pass 'tool-improver' so provenance stays honest. Confirm that source value is acceptable to rerender-pages' claim query.
4) create_rerender_items only stamps and scopes when reason is section_data_resolved/image_landed AND component_id is present (create_rerender_items_action.go:136-140) — both hold here, but that coupling is what the whole chain rests on.
5) Go changes are inert until a chassis image is rebuilt and rolled; edit 3 is live immediately, so applying 171 BEFORE the image ships would remove the only (broken) rerender request and leave none. Sequence: image first, then 171.
6) Not fixed here, deliberately: insertWorkItem's two-strike rule counting 'complete' as a failed attempt (load_work_item_actions.go:1019) and create_work_item's site-wide item_key (create_work_item_action.go:128). Both real, both filed in bugs_open/024, neither on this change's path.
